steps.title: Prepare 0.1 M phosphate buffer
steps.instruction: Make 0.1 M PB by mixing monobasic and dibasic sodium phosphate, adjust pH, filter and store.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 0.6 g sodium phosphate monobasic (MW = 119.98 g·mol⁻¹) in 50 mL ultrapure water (solution A) while stirring.
Dissolve 2.4 g sodium phosphate dibasic (MW = 141.96 g·mol⁻¹) in 170 mL ultrapure water (solution B) while stirring.
Slowly pour solution A into solution B with continuous stirring, monitor pH and stop when pH reaches 7.3–7.4.
Filter the mixed solution through a sterile bottle‑top filter.
Store at 4 °C for up to one month.

steps.title: Prepare 0.5 M phosphate buffer
steps.instruction: Make 0.5 M PB using higher concentrations of the same salts, adjust pH, filter and store.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 3 g sodium phosphate monobasic in 50 mL ultrapure water (solution A) while stirring.
Dissolve 12 g sodium phosphate dibasic in 170 mL ultrapure water (solution B) while stirring.
Slowly add solution A to solution B, stir and monitor pH until it reaches 7.3–7.4.
Filter through a sterile bottle‑top filter.
Store at 4 °C for up to one month.

steps.title: Prepare 4 % PFA fixative
steps.instruction: Dissolve paraformaldehyde in warm water, adjust pH, add 0.5 M PB, filter and store.

substeps.instruction: In a chemical fume hood, measure 70 mL ultrapure water and heat to 55–60 °C on a hot‑plate stirrer (do not exceed 65 °C).
Slowly add 4 g paraformaldehyde while stirring.
Add 1 N NaOH drop‑by‑drop until the solution clears.
Allow the solution to cool to room temperature.
Add 20 mL of 0.5 M phosphate buffer (prepared above) and bring the final volume to 100 mL.
Adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 N HCl or 1 N NaOH as needed.
Filter through a sterile bottle‑top filter.
Store at 4 °C for up to one week, or aliquot 50 mL portions and keep at –20 °C for up to one month.

steps.title: Prepare Avertin anesthetic
steps.instruction: Dissolve tribromoethanol in 2‑methyl‑2‑butanol, dilute with water, filter and store in light‑protected aliquots.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 250 mg 2,2,2‑tribromoethanol (44 mM) in 0.5 mL 2‑methyl‑2‑butanol while stirring at 40 °C (do not exceed 40 °C).
Add ultrapure water to bring the total volume to 20 mL.
Filter the solution with a sterile 0.22 µm syringe filter.
Aliquot into 0.5 mL portions, store at –20 °C for up to one year in amber/brown tubes protected from light.
Do not refreeze unused aliquots; discard and remake if the solution is past its one‑year expiration, turns yellow, or begins to crystallize.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse and set up perfusion
steps.instruction: Weigh the animal, inject Avertin, position the mouse, and prepare the perfusion pump with PBS and PFA.

substeps.instruction: Weigh the mouse (e.g., 10 g).
Inject intraperitoneally Avertin at 250 mg·kg⁻¹ body weight.
Place the mouse supine on a dissection tray and secure limbs with clamps or laboratory tape.
In a chemical fume hood, pour ice‑cold 0.1 M PB and 4 % PFA into separate glass beakers and connect each to the perfusion pump.
Prefill all tubing with the respective solutions, remove air bubbles, and connect a three‑way stopcock to the PB line, the PFA line, and the injection needle.

steps.title: Transcardial perfusion with PBS
steps.instruction: Flush the circulatory system with ice‑cold PBS until blood is cleared.

substeps.instruction: Make a midline abdominal incision caudal to the rib cage, cut through the diaphragm, and open the thoracic cavity.
Cut laterally along the rib cage to expose the heart; locate the left ventricle and right atrium.
Insert a 25‑gauge needle into the caudal portion of the left ventricle at a flat angle, avoiding the septum.
Make a small incision in the right atrium with scissors to allow rapid outflow.
Turn on the pump and flush ice‑cold 0.1 M PB through the left ventricle at 1–2 mL·min⁻¹, securing the needle with modeling clay or tape.
Continue flushing until the volume injected equals three times the mouse’s body weight (e.g., 30 mL for a 10 g mouse) and the effluent from the right atrium is clear.
Confirm liver color change from dark red to pale yellow/white.

steps.title: Perfusion with 4 % PFA fixative
steps.instruction: Replace PBS with fixative and perfuse until tissues stiffen.

substeps.instruction: Using the three‑way stopcock, switch the pump line to 4 % PFA, ensuring no air bubbles remain.
Maintain the needle position in the left ventricle and inject at least three times the mouse’s body weight (e.g., 30 mL for a 10 g mouse).
Observe stiffening of organs and limbs after a few minutes.
Stop the pump, remove the needle, and decapitate the animal with surgical scissors.

steps.title: Brain dissection and post‑fixation
steps.instruction: Extract the brain, remove meninges, and post‑fix overnight then transfer to PBS.

substeps.instruction: Carefully remove the brain from the skull, avoiding contact with the region of interest (e.g., cochlear nucleus or MNTB).
Cut larger nerves with fine scissors rather than tearing them.
Using forceps, gently peel the meninges from the ventral surface of the brainstem.
Place the brain in a 12‑well plate containing 4 % PFA (volume ≥3× brain volume; >1.5 mL for an adult mouse brain) and incubate at 4 °C overnight.
After 12 h, discard the PFA solution and replace with 0.1 M PBS (same minimum volume).
Keep the brain submerged in PBS at 4 °C; use within a few hours for best fluorescence (storage for several days reduces signal).

steps.title: Slice brain and mount sections
steps.instruction: Section the fixed brain at 40 µm, collect slices, and mount with mounting medium.

substeps.instruction: Remove the brain from PBS and excise the rostral half of the cerebrum with a razor blade.
Apply a small amount of super‑glue to the cut surface and attach the brain to a specimen holder, avoiding contact with the brainstem.
Immerse the holder in PBS and orient it so the ventral brainstem surface faces the vibrating microtome blade.
Slice at 40 µm thickness, moving the blade at 20–50 µm·s⁻¹.
Collect slices containing the region of interest in PBS.
Mount each slice on a microscope slide, remove excess PBS, and let the slice dry almost completely.
Add one drop of Aqua‑Poly/Mount to each dried slice, avoiding air bubbles, and cover with a cover glass.
Allow the mounting medium to harden for 24 h at room temperature.
Store completed slides at 4 °C in the dark; they remain usable for several months and can be imaged repeatedly.

steps.title: Confocal imaging of calyx terminals
steps.instruction: Acquire high‑resolution 3‑D stacks of EGFP‑labeled calyx terminals using a 63× oil objective.

substeps.instruction: Locate the MNTB region on a low‑magnification objective and select isolated EGFP‑positive calyx terminals.
Switch to a 63× oil immersion objective (Plan‑Apochromat 63×/1.4 Oil DIC M27).
Set excitation to 488 nm and emission to 518 nm.
Choose Scan Mode = Frame, image size = 1024 × 1024 pixels.
Set Speed = 8, Averaging = 4 lines, Bit Depth = 16‑bit, Scan Mode = Bidirectional.
Define pixel dimensions as 0.1 µm × 0.1 µm × 0.35 µm (x, y, z).
Adjust laser power, gain, and offset so that the signal is within detector range, background is low, contrast is high, and no pixels are saturated.
Image the entire presynaptic terminal plus at least 5 µm on each side in the z‑axis.

steps.title: 3D reconstruction in Imaris
steps.instruction: Generate a surface model of each calyx terminal from the confocal z‑stack using manual segmentation.

substeps.instruction: Start Imaris, open the Arena, and drag‑and‑drop the acquired z‑stack file into the Arena.
Double‑click the file to convert it to IMS format, then open the IMS file.
In 3D View, locate a well‑isolated calyx that is fully captured; choose Edit > Crop 3D and crop the volume with ~1 µm margins around the terminal, then click OK.
In the Surpass tree, select Add new Surfaces, then select the newly created surface object.
In the Create tab, choose “Skip automatic creation, edit manually”. Click Settings and enable “Render on Slicer”.
Use the Slice Position slider to display a middle slice where the calyx is clearly visible.
In the Drawing Mode tab, select Magic Wand and click Draw; the software will generate line‑bound surfaces of uniform pixel intensity.
Adjust vertices by holding the T key and clicking, delete unwanted vertices with the D key, and refine the surface to match the calyx dimensions.
Move to the next slice using the Slice Position slider and repeat the drawing and adjustment steps for every slice until the entire terminal is segmented.
Click “Create Surface” at the bottom of the Draw tab, then turn off “Render on Slicer”.
In the Edit tab, inspect the surface; if multiple surfaces belong to the same terminal, select them and click the Unify button.
Open the Statistics tab, select “Selection”, choose “Specific Values”, and check “Area” and “Volume”.
Export the measurements to CSV or XLS using the Export Statistics button.
